scope: Authoritative starting documents for food-form distinctions, edible fraction/yields, and nutrient retention. This index does not establish recipe-specific transformations or finished mixed-recipe nutrition.

massYield.definition: Prepared mass divided by input mass for an expressly matching food and preparation.

edibleFraction.definition: Edible portion divided by as-acquired mass, with refuse/form basis stated.

nutrientRetention.definition: Nutrient amount retained after a matching preparation, distinct from mass yield and edible fraction.

verifiedFindings: The PDF identifies itself as Release 6, prepared by USDA ARS Nutrient Data Laboratory, dated December 2007.
The document describes nutrient-specific retention factors for selected vitamins, minerals, and alcohol across food/preparation categories.
Its true-retention method uses nutrient concentrations and food weights before and after cooking; the document notes factors can be imputed where data are limited.
sources.applicability: Potential reference for a nutrient-retention transform only where the exact food group, nutrient, and preparation category match after row-level review.

sources.title: USDA Food Buying Guide for Child Nutrition Programs — Yield Tables and Methods
sources.publicationDate: Dynamic guide; consulted page lists dated table updates. Grains yield table last updated 2026-03-25; meats/meat-alternates 2026-09-02.
sources.license: Document/page reuse license unknown; any stated FDC data license applies to datasets, not automatically to documentation PDFs or site text.
verifiedFindings: USDA describes yields as average yields based on its research and as planning/production guidance.
Tables distinguish food as purchased, purchase unit, edible-portion servings, serving form, and additional cooked/ready-to-use quantities.
The download index exposes separate grains and meats yield tables with stated update dates; its methods page gives examples for raw-to-cooked ground beef and cooked grains/rice.
sources.applicability: A possible exact-form yield starting point for listed institutional foods such as grains/rice and meats, after checking the actual table row and purchase/preparation assumptions.
sources.limitations: Designed for U.S. child-nutrition purchasing and serving. Average planning yields are not interchangeable with ingredient mass yield, refuse fraction, or nutrient retention. No factors extracted. It does not establish bechamel, pasta, or any finished mixed recipe yield; proxy cuisine is not claimed.
